title: Slot utilization & client-tier sensitivity
summary: Working spreadsheet to quantify how GPU slot utilization and SKU mix across customer tiers (free/dev, standard, enterprise) drive per-token COGS and margin. The file modelled slot occupancy, average batch size by tier, cache hit-rate scenarios, and fallback frequency to cheaper/expensive model variants to produce sensitivity curves for PPK and gross margin.
assumptions: GPU slot = 1x A100-40GB equivalent; cost amortized monthly with license & infra; base slot cost = $11,500/month per slot
Active sessions per slot proportional to average batch size; effective throughput = batches_per_slot * avg_tokens_per_batch
Model families simplified to: L1 (small, low cost), L2 (medium), L3 (large); relative token cost multipliers: 0.5 / 1 / 2.7
Cache hit rates evaluated at 0%, 15%, 35%, 60% (prefix & KV cache combined)
Fallback routing: 4% of requests fall back to regional reserve variants under 95th percentile load in baseline
Regional p50 latency SLO targets influence reserved batch size and therefore utilization (higher latency SLO => higher batch sizes permitted)
Overhead: 6% request-level infra overhead (network, orchestration) added to raw GPU COGS
sample_rows: Row example: tier=standard | concurrency=1200/day | avg_batch=2.2 | tokens_per_req=280 | model_mix=L2:70% L3:30% | cache_hit=28% => slot_needed=12.8 | amortized_slot_cost_per_token=$0.000013
Row example: tier=enterprise | concurrency=4,800/day | avg_batch=3.6 | tokens_per_req=520 | model_mix=L2:45% L3:55% | cache_hit=8% => slot_needed=58.3 | amortized_slot_cost_per_token=$0.000021
Row example: tier=free/dev | concurrency=2,400/day | avg_batch=1.1 | tokens_per_req=120 | model_mix=L1:85% L2:15% | cache_hit=60% => slot_needed=7.1 | amortized_slot_cost_per_token=$0.000004
key_findings: Short-run utilization swings (p95 burst windows) force holding ~18% more slots than steady-state to meet latency SLOs; that overhead alone increases blended PPK by ~9-12% depending on model mix.

Cache improvements from 15% to 35% reduce total monthly slot requirement by ~11% for workloads dominated by repeat prompts (chat/assistant), translating to ~7-9% margin expansion at current price points.
Shifting 10% of enterprise requests from L3->L2 as a graceful degrade yields larger unit cost relief than a uniform 5% cache improvement for latency-sensitive tiers in baseline regions.
Batch size sensitivity: for standard tier, increasing avg batch from 1.8 to 2.6 reduces per-token GPU cost by ~14%, but increases tail latency; A/B test recommended before rolling broadly.
Regional variance: APAC GPU slot effective cost premium +18% vs NA drives notable margin compression for model-heavy workloads — consider region-specific pricing or routing policies for cost parity.
recommendations: Short-term (1-2 months): introduce a 'cache-boost' experiment for top 10 enterprise customers (enable aggressive prefix sharing and per-customer KV caches); measure slot reduction and update per-customer PPK.

Medium-term (3-6 months): add a per-tier degrade policy allowing controlled L3->L2 fallback for non-critical completions during burst; expose as a product toggle in Console with estimated savings shown.
Operational: create a per-region slot-reserve buffer calculation that factors in p95 burst and a configurable safety factor (default 1.18). Surface this metric in the Dedicated capacity planner.
Pricing: pilot a regionally-differentiated enterprise SLA surcharge (APAC premium) or offer guaranteed lower p95 for higher commit tiers to preserve margins.
Engineering: prioritize batching improvements in serving-runtime for small-req regimes (micro-batching heuristics) to safely increase batch size without tail-latency regressions.
Product: update hosted API docs with recommended prompt patterns to increase cacheability and provide SDK helpers for deterministic caching keys.
constraints_and_open_questions: How will stricter GDPR-like data residency rules affect cross-region fallback options for enterprise customers (may block routing to lower-cost regions)?
Need REMOTE question: how accurate are current customer-provided concurrency profiles vs observed telemetry — dataset mismatch was ~12% in last audit
What is the expected engineering effort and risk vector for per-tenant prefix cache isolation? (security vs savings tradeoff)
Should billing reflect observed slot-efficiency (e.g., rebate/credit when cache reduction materially lowers our costs)?
notes_to_deck: Use the sensitivity grid on tab 'Sensitivity grid: PPK vs utilization' for the executive slide. Highlight two concrete wins: (1) cache-boost pilot with top 10 enterprise customers projected to reduce 3-5 slots each; (2) L3->L2 degrade pilot projected to recover ~12% margin on heavy-model routes. Flag regionally differentiated pricing as a decision point.
